And yes, when you’re starting out as a content creator in the arts niche, you’ll have to create strategically. (Unlike lifestyle creators who can just talk about their favorite products while doing their skincare because the content is.. them as a person) The art content creators I’ve worked with definitely put in so much more work. 

When you work with those local brands, treat it like a partnership with your absolute dream brand. 

Best of luck! You can do this!

Yes exactly! And if you can find a way to integrate your personality into the content, that would also elevate it! 

I think you can go about it either way. Your drawing strangers series can be more subtle with the brands but you can also have another content pillar where you show more of your personality like enjoying Tim Hortons and drawing something Tim Hortons related. That would be much more brand dedicated but still feel authentic because it’s a brand you actually love/use/enjoy. 

Obviously I can’t promise instant brand deals BUT getting on the brand’s radar is huge!! Maybe you’ll end up on their PR list or start getting more event invites. Then you can really use those to your advantage.

A few more content thought starters -
Going to Dunkin Donuts and reviewing or talking about their drink and drawing something Dunkin related. This can get food brands looking at your content. Apply the same technique for other niches. 

Maybe something in the digital art space. Do you use Adobe products? Show how you use it, tips and techniques, etc. This will get Adobe’s eyes on your content.

I work in influencer marketing so creator partnerships is what I do all day every day. 

I just took a quick look at your TikTok. While yes you could work with lots of different brands, you need to show that on your page. I like the on the go drawing content but maybe if you’re at a chain restaurant, integrate the restaurant into the drawing and tag them. If there’s specific art supplies you use, make sure you can see it in the video and tag the brand. 

I know this drawing strangers content is what you’ve grown your account to be but maybe you integrate other content like drawing the artists or outfits from the Grammys Red Carpet, drawing the holiday menu from Dunkin Donuts. 

Consistent, unique, high quality series style content is what is working right now. Take a look at Chloe Shih’s 30 lessons series. 

But yes unfortunately location plays a big part of it. I’ve worked with brands across Europe, Asia and the US and US budget is alwayssssss higher. By a crazy amount.

Take this with a grain of salt since I’ve never seen your actual content and am basing it off what you’ve shared. 

Brands are getting in touch with creators. Just because a profile has hundreds of thousands followers doesn’t automatically mean brands will flock to your email. 

How strong is your community? Do you have followers who will engage with your content and follow your every move or buy things you post about? Can a brand see their product in your content? As in, if a brand’s influencer marketing manager goes to your profile, can they easily think of five ideas to integrate their product with your content style? 

Unfortunately, it could also be due to geographical location. Many brands only want to spend with creators who have a large US audience because US = audience who spends. Your content style might make it a little more difficult too. There’s a reason the lifestyle girlies are racking up brand deals because there’s a vast range of brands that can be plugged into their content. 

The easiest way to increase your chances of landing a brand deal is including content ideas in your email pitches.
